Subject: HIPAA: PHI handling and BAA eligibility — quick questions

Hi Rachel / HealthNet legal —

Thanks again for taking the time on Friday. To make sure we scope the work correctly I had a couple of clarifying questions about the PHI flow that will determine eligibility for a Redwood BAA and the recommended deployment model:

- What exact categories of PHI will be transmitted to the inference endpoint? (e.g., patient name, MRN, full clinical notes, DICOM attachments)
- Will HealthNet send attachments (images, PDFs) to be processed through the model?
- Do you expect us to persist user prompts or extracted outputs long-term for analytics or auditing?

High level on our side: Redwood offers Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private deployments. Our security team generally recommends Dedicated or Private for PHI, but if the PHI flow is strictly transient and you have strict non-retention requirements we may be able to evaluate a hosted exception with additional controls.

I've attached a short spreadsheet with our common questions to speed the review. Can you confirm the PHI types and whether the environment that will call the API is under HealthNet's VPC or from internet-facing systems?

Proposed next step: a 30-min security call this week with our security lead and legal to go over controls and the BAA template. Are you available Wed or Thu afternoon PT?

Thanks,

Thanks for the ping — technical summary:

- Hosted API: telemetry and minimal request metadata are collected for platform health by default. We have an opt-out and retention controls but Hosted is not our recommended path for processing PHI because customers cannot currently enforce full data isolation or customer-managed KMS across the multi-tenant control plane.
- Dedicated/Private: supports customer-managed KMS, strict network isolation (VPC peering), audit logging with per-token traces, and can be configured to disable persistent request/response logging. This is the model we recommend for PHI.
- Attachments: PDFs and images can be relayed, but we recommend performing pre-processing in the customer environment (redact PII) before sending to inference.

Action items for sales/legal: if HealthNet requires BAA coverage, we should propose Dedicated or Private. I'll prepare a short control matrix (SOC2, encryption details, sub-processors) and share it with legal for the BAA draft.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Security & Compliance Lead, Redwood Inference

Team —

Legal position and proposed path forward:

- Redwood can execute a BAA, but we limit BAA-covered processing to Dedicated and Private deployments where we can guarantee contractual controls (KMS, network isolation, logging configuration).
- We cannot reasonably accept PHI under our standard multi-tenant Hosted product without additional contractual assurances and engineering changes; that would require an exception review and longer timeline.
- Next steps: provide HealthNet with our BAA draft, latest SOC 2 letter, sub-processor registry, encryption at rest/in-transit summary, and an outline of audit logging capabilities. Ask them to confirm whether they prefer Dedicated or Private and propose dates for a security architecture call.

Evelyn Hart
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
